verified_signals.signal: ACCESSIBILITY GAP CONFIRMED, LEGAL DEADLINE CONTRADICTED. The gap is real and I re-measured it: only 376 of 1,096 BCR ATMs (34%) carry the VOICE (audio guidance) tag, against 572 of 573 MFMs (99.8%); 73 ATMs are not tagged contactless. About 720 BCR ATMs therefore have no audio guidance. Romania's Law 232/2022 (Monitorul Oficial I nr. 743 of 25/07/2022, in force 28/06/2025), which transposes the EU Accessibility Act (Directive 2019/882), expressly covers ATMs ('bancomate' as self-service payment terminals, Art. 2) and requires self-service terminals to provide text-to-speech and support personal headphones (Annex 1). BUT THE RESEARCHER'S 28/06/2030 CLIFF IS WRONG. Art. 29(2) of Law 232/2022 states, verbatim, that self-service terminals used by service providers before 28/06/2025 may continue in use for similar services 'dar nu mai mult de 20 de ani dupa intrarea lor in uz' - no more than 20 years after entry into use. Art. 29(1), which carries the 28/06/2030 date, opens 'Prin exceptie de la prevederile alin. (2)', i.e. it is expressly subordinated to the self-service-terminal rule. Romania took the Member State option in Art. 32(2) of the Directive. So there is NO 2030 replacement cliff for BCR's legacy ATMs; the binding constraint is (a) every terminal placed on the market/put into use from 28/06/2025 must be accessible, and (b) each legacy machine ages out 20 years after ITS OWN entry into use. Peer pressure is nonetheless real: Raiffeisen Bank Romania stated in its Q1-2026 release (04/05/2026) that voice guidance for cash withdrawal at ATMs and MFMs was 'extinsa la nivel national' - extended nationwide.
verified_signals.source_name: Law 232/2022 Art. 29 (Lege5 reproduction of the Monitorul Oficial text) and Directive (EU) 2019/882 Art. 32 (EUR-Lex); BCR locator API
verified_signals.implies: Roughly 720 BCR ATMs cannot serve blind and partially sighted customers today, against a direct competitor that says it has gone nationwide. That is a reputational and procurement driver, and every unit BCR replaces from now on must ship compliant (text-to-speech, headphone jack) - so accessibility rides on the refresh cycle rather than forcing it. Sellable as an audio/software retrofit where the hardware allows, and as a compliance argument inside any ATM/MFM replacement tender. It is NOT a legally dated 2030 refresh pipeline, and it should not be pitched as one.
verified_signals.likelihood: Retrofit-or-replace decisions likely tied to normal refresh and to competitive/reputational pressure, not to a statutory 2030 date
verified_signals.followup: Establish whether the 720 non-voice ATMs are software/audio-jack upgradeable or need a hardware swap, and get their entry-into-use dates - under Art. 29(2) that date, not 2030, sets each machine's legal end of life. Look for any published BCR accessibility remediation plan (none found this run).
verified_signals.verifier_note: CONTRADICTED ON THE DEADLINE - this was the single biggest error in the pass. I opened the Law 232/2022 text and the Directive itself rather than trusting the summary. Directive 2019/882 Art. 32(1) gives a transitional period 'ending on 28 June 2030' for service providers using legacy products, but it opens 'Without prejudice to paragraph 2', and Art. 32(2) lets Member States allow self-service terminals used before 28/06/2025 to run 'until the end of their economically useful life, but no longer than 20 years after their entry into use'. Romania exercised that option: Law 232/2022 Art. 29(2) reads 'Terminalele pentru autoservire utilizate de catre furnizorii de servicii pentru furnizarea de servicii inainte de 28 iunie 2025 pot sa fie utilizate in continuare pentru furnizarea de servicii similare, dar nu mai mult de 20 de ani dupa intrarea lor in uz', and Art. 29(1) is drafted as an exception FROM 29(2). The researcher's 'continue only until 28/06/2030' is therefore materially wrong, and I removed the 28/06/2030 deadline and downgraded opp_size from XL to L because the forced-refresh mechanism that justified XL does not exist. The 376/1,096 and 572/573 voice counts I re-measured from my own API pull and they are correct. The Raiffeisen claim I checked against this run's verified raiffeisen-ro file, which quotes the Q1-2026 BVB filing verbatim ('A fost extinsa la nivel national functionalitatea de ghidare vocala pentru retragerile de numerar la ATM-uri si MFM-uri'); I re-dated it to the 04/05/2026 release rather than 'completed in Q1 2026'. Note also that Law 232/2022 was published 25/07/2022 and entered force 28/06/2025 - it is standing law, not a 2026 development.

BCR's own numbers were unchanged at 31/03/2026, so the entire step down (-250 devices, -12.5%; -6 branches; -1 business centre; -3 mobile offices) appears in the Q2 2026 disclosure - one quarter, not two. verified_signals.signal: DERIVED OFF-SITE PERIMETER (analysis, not a BCR announcement). Matching device coordinates to branch coordinates at 4 decimal places on my own 31/07/2026 API pull: 782 of 1,096 ATMs (71%) sit away from any BCR branch, versus 169 of 573 MFMs (29%). ATMs appear in 383 towns and MFMs in 173, against 157 towns with a branch - so the off-site ATM estate is what gives BCR coverage in roughly 226 towns where it has no branch.
verified_signals.source_name: BCR locator API, verifier's own derived analysis
verified_signals.implies: An off-site estate of roughly 780 ATMs across 383 towns is exactly the asset class regional peers have handed to a partner. Two such precedents are independently verified in this same run: Raiffeisen Bank Romania's own locator carries 595 Euronet-branded devices alongside its 1,211 own-branded ones, and Payten bought 122 externally-sited ATMs from Banca Intesa Beograd on a 36-month contract with a full Diebold Nixdorf replacement in year one. That makes BCR's off-site ATMs the most sellable managed-services / ATM-as-a-service perimeter - and the perimeter most exposed to being taken by a rival deployer.
verified_signals.likelihood: Speculative. No BCR statement of any outsourcing intent exists; this is a target perimeter derived from geography, not a disclosed plan
verified_signals.followup: Coordinate matching is approximate - lobby devices geocoded a few metres from the branch pin will read as off-site, so treat 782/169 as an order of magnitude and validate against BCR's own on-site/off-site split. Watch for any BCR RFI on ATM operations.
verified_signals.verifier_note: I re-ran the derivation from scratch on my own pull and reproduced the researcher's numbers exactly: 782 off-site ATMs of 1,096, 169 off-site MFMs of 573, 383 ATM towns / 173 MFM towns / 157 branch towns. The arithmetic is sound. What I tightened is the framing: the researcher presented this alongside four peer precedents (Piraeus to Cashflex/Printec, Banca Intesa to Payten, Raiffeisen Romania to Euronet, CrediaBank to Euronet). I checked the two Romanian/Serbian ones against this run's own verified files - raiffeisen-ro.json (595 Euronet devices inside Raiffeisen's locator, verification 'confirmed') and banca-intesa-rs.json (122 ATMs, 36-month Payten contract, verification 'confirmed'). The Piraeus and CrediaBank precedents I did NOT re-verify in this pass and I have dropped them from the text rather than pass them through unchecked. verified_signals.signal: ROBOR COMPETITION CASE. Erste Group's H1 2026 interim report, note 31, states that on 06/04/2026 BCR received an investigation report from the Romanian Competition Council alleging agreements and/or concerted practice on coordinated fixing of the ROBOR reference rate among the ten panel banks, covering the period since November 2018; that in early June 2026 the Council publicly announced a fine on BCR of 6.1875% of its 2025 turnover = RON 577,361,887 (~EUR 110m); that the reasoned decision had not been served on BCR; and that BCR will contest it by all available legal means. BCR published its own statements on 08/06/2026 ('Respingem constatarile acesteia si ne vom apara cu fermitate') and 11/06/2026, the latter alleging the Council refused adequate access to the case file and reasonable time to respond. Romanian press reports sector-wide sanctions of RON 3.73bn (~EUR 710m) across ten banks and the National Bank of Romania publicly questioning the decision on financial-stability grounds; those cross-bank figures are press-only and are not in any primary document I could open.
verified_signals.source_name: Erste Group Interim Report H1 2026 note 31; BCR press statements 08/06/2026 and 11/06/2026
verified_signals.implies: A ~EUR 110m provisionable exposure plus a multi-year appeal, on top of an already deteriorating cost/income ratio. For Printec this is a budget-climate driver and a governance signal - the auditability bar on any outsourced service will be higher - rather than a product opening. The conduct at issue is benchmark submission, not payments fraud, so the read-across to AML/transaction-monitoring is weak and should not be oversold.
verified_signals.likelihood: Litigation certain; any compliance-spend uplift is speculative
verified_signals.followup: Track service of the reasoned decision and BCR's court challenge. Resolve one open discrepancy: Erste says the alleged conduct runs 'since November 2018', while Romanian press coverage describes a 2007-2012 manipulation period - the reasoned decision will settle it.
verified_signals.verifier_note: I downloaded the 1.7 MB Erste interim report and read note 31 in full. (1) The researcher noted consiliulconcurentei.ro was unreachable and left the case resting on Erste alone; I found and read two BCR primary statements the pass missed - 08/06/2026 and 11/06/2026 on bcr.ro - which independently confirm the decision and add the due-process complaint. The RON 3.73bn / EUR 710m sector total and the BNR reaction are corroborated across several Romanian outlets but not in any primary document, so I labelled them as press-only inside the signal rather than dropping them.

verified_signals.signal: REMITTANCE AT THE MACHINE, DOCUMENTED BY BCR ITSELF. MoneyGram send-and-receive is enabled on 572 of 573 BCR multifunctional machines per the locator's own service tags, and BCR's public product page describes the full flow: the customer gets a QR code valid six months at a branch, then at a 'Ghiseu Multifunctional' scans the QR, enters an OTP sent by SMS, selects PRIMESTE BANI, enters the MoneyGram reference and takes cash and a receipt - explicitly 'fara sa ai cont deschis la BCR', i.e. without holding a BCR account. Separately, contactless card withdrawal is on all 573 MFMs and 1,023 of 1,096 ATMs, while EUR withdrawal is on only 320 ATMs and 13 MFMs.
verified_signals.source_name: BCR MoneyGram product page (bcr.ro) and BCR locator API service tags
verified_signals.implies: BCR already monetises the self-service channel beyond own-customer cash: a fee-bearing, identity-verified remittance for non-customers, executed on the machine. That is the strongest available argument for MFM density and for value-added application software on the terminal - a Printec multivendor-software and managed-services angle rather than a hardware pitch. The friction is visible too: enrolment still needs a branch visit and an appointment, which is itself an onboarding/eKYC opening.
verified_signals.followup: Check whether the MoneyGram integration sits in the ATM application layer (retrofittable to the ~1,096 cash-out ATMs, which would multiply the addressable transaction base) or only on the MFM platform. Also probe whether the branch-visit QR enrolment step could be moved onto the machine or into an eKYC flow.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Tag counts re-measured on my own pull: MONEYGRAM 572 of 573 MFMs, CONTACTLESS 573/573 and 1,023/1,096, EUR 320 ATMs and 13 MFMs - all match the researcher exactly. verified_signals.signal: IT INVESTMENT PROXY, now fully sourced. Audited FY2025 accounts, Note 33 'Imobilizari necorporale' (Group, thousand RON): gross additions rose to RON 149,759k in 2025 from RON 132,589k in 2024 (+12.9%), split purchased software RON 95,076k, Group-developed software RON 50,447k and licences RON 4,236k. Gross intangible cost reached RON 1,534,125k at 31/12/2025. Software and licences are amortised straight-line over 5-10 years, with licences amortised over their period of use. RON 149.8m is roughly EUR 30m.
verified_signals.source_name: BCR Raport anual 2025, Note 33 Imobilizari necorporale (BVB infocont filing)
verified_signals.implies: About EUR 30m a year of capitalised software, growing 13% y/y, on a 5-10 year amortisation life. That sets a realistic ceiling for a software-led engagement and shows BCR capitalises rather than expenses software - so a licence-plus-implementation structure that can be capitalised is easier to land on the software side, even though the hardware/service side favours opex. Note also that a third of the additions are Group-developed, i.e. built inside Erste, which is the internal competitor for any software proposal.
verified_signals.likelihood: Run-rate plausibly maintained in 2026 on the two-year trend; no BCR IT budget is published
verified_signals.followup: Re-read Note 33 in the FY2026 report (due around March 2027) to see whether the purchased-vs-Group-developed mix shifts further in-house.

verified_signals.entity: Romanian ATM and POS market (context for BCR)
verified_signals.signal: MARKET CONTEXT - PRESS-SOURCED, NOT VERIFIED AT THE REGULATOR. BURSA, reporting BNR payment statistics via Agerpres, states that at 31/12/2025 resident payment service providers had 11,136 ATMs deployed (+1,108 versus June 2025), 729,408 POS terminals (+161,396) and 685,731 EFTPOS acceptance points (+120,300), with 28.63 million active cards (+10.07% vs June 2025) of which 24.68 million have a cash function. TREAT THE ATM NUMBER WITH CAUTION: +1,108 ATMs in six months is roughly +11% on the national estate, which is implausibly fast as organic deployment and may reflect a change in reporting scope or in which deployers are counted. I could not reach the BNR table itself to check.
verified_signals.source_name: BURSA, reporting BNR payment statistics via Agerpres
verified_signals.implies: If the figures hold, the national ATM estate grew in H2 2025 while BCR's shrank in Q2 2026, so BCR is ceding physical cash-access share - which both pressures BCR to defend coverage cheaply (managed services, off-site partnership) and opens white space for independent deployers. BCR's ~1,750 devices would be roughly 16% of the national estate. POS growth of 161k in six months is the parallel POS/acquiring opportunity. None of this should be quoted to a client until the BNR table is read directly.
verified_signals.likelihood: Unverified. The divergence is plausible but rests on a single press report of a regulator dataset I could not open
verified_signals.followup: Read the BNR statistics directly - the interactive database at bnr.ro/1074-baza-de-date-interactiva is JavaScript-driven and the ECB Data Portal PSS API rejected the query this run, so this needs a browser session or the published BNR payments statistics release. Until then do not build a market-share argument on it.
verified_signals.verifier_note: I opened the BURSA article and it does state all five figures verbatim ('la 31 decembrie 2025, numarul de ATM-uri furnizate de PSP rezidenti ... era de 11.136 (plus 1.108 comparativ cu iunie 2025), cel de POS de 729.408 (+161.396) ... 685.731 (+120.300)', '28,63 milioane ... in crestere cu 10,07%', '24,68 milioane aveau functie de numerar'), so the researcher transcribed it correctly. But the article is press reporting Agerpres reporting BNR, and I could NOT reach the regulator source: bnr.ro's payment-statistics pages resolve to a portal whose interactive database is JS-rendered, and the ECB Data Portal PSS endpoint returned HTTP 400. Under the aggregator rule I dropped confidence to Low and set verification 'unconfirmed'. I also downgraded opp_size from L to Unscoped - this is macro context, not a sized BCR opportunity - and added an explicit plausibility warning on the +11% six-month ATM jump, which the researcher passed through without comment and which is the number a client is most likely to challenge.

I got the annual report only via WebFetch, and the file returned is byte-identical to the researcher's (MD5 ea847958b13ef60e20bc31a49a90c76b), which is why Note 33 and the network paragraph could be confirmed. The 11,136-ATM national figure therefore remains press-only and is marked Low/unconfirmed. (3) consiliulconcurentei.ro was not retried - Erste's interim report and BCR's own 08/06 and 11/06/2026 statements carry the case with more precision. (4) BCR's FY2025 results PDF on the erstegroup CDN is vector/outlined text; only the financial tables extract, so the FY2025 network paragraph was taken from the audited annual report instead, where it is intact. OPEN QUESTIONS THAT ARE NOT SOURCING FAILURES. (a) The ATM/MFM hardware OEM at BCR is still unidentified in any public source - I re-ran targeted searches for Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Hyosung and Printec against BCR for 2019-2026 and found nothing beyond the 2017 NCR/Printec cash-management story; this is the single most valuable unknown. (c) The 81-unit gap between BCR's disclosed 1,750 devices and the locator's 1,669 records is unexplained - most likely restricted-access or newly-deployed machines omitted from the public locator, but it is a guess and is labelled as such.
